To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the plasma membrane of the cellular slime mould D. discoideium can be purified by a simple procedure that involves freeze-thawing of the cells, followed by equilibrium density-gradient centrifugation and that the isolated plasma membrane contains three distinct subfractions of differing densities that can be separated by isopycic centrifugation.
we have isolated and subfractionated the plasma membrane from the amoeboid stage of the cellular slime mould D. discoideun and have shown that it is a smooth vesicular structure.
the plasma membrane of Dictyostelium can be purified and that alkaline phosphatases are localized to a particular subfraction of the plasma membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and subfraction of plasma membrane from Dictyostelium.
the isolation of a plasma-membranous fraction from the cellular slime mold Dictyostelium discoidum which is enriched in alkaline phosphatases.
the development of a procedure for the isolation of plasma membrane from Dictyostelium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the subfraction with a density of 1.11 g/ml contains the highest specific activity of alkaline phosphodiesterase and is the best subfraction for the isolation of plasma membrane from Dictyostelium.
this is the most complete and successful procedure for the preparation and separation of plasma-membrane fractions in D. discoideaum to date.
the procedure described here is suitable for the isolation of plasma membrane from Dictyostelium.

we have obtained a preparation of D. discoideium plasma membranes that is enriched 36-fold in alkaline phosphatases, and that this enrichment is achieved with a minimum contamination by other membranes.
the isolation and subfraction of plasma membranes from D. discoideium is a simple, rapid and reproducible procedure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plasma membranes of Dictyostelium cells are enriched in alkaline phosphatases and are not associated with the 5'-nucleotidase enzyme, as is the case with mammalian cells.
the subfractionation of the plasma membrane is possible, and the subfractionation can be used to study the properties of different regions of the membrane.
D. discoideun is a good model organism to study plasma membrane proteins and the plasma membrane is a great organelle for membrane protein biogenesis studies.
